subject: Physics
detected_problem_latex: Find the electric field at point $P(r, \theta)$ due to a short electric dipole of dipole moment $\vec{p}$.
error_analysis: The student applied the axial field formula $E = \frac{2kp}{r^3}$ instead of the general position formula $E = \frac{kp}{r^3}\sqrt{1 + 3\cos^2\theta}$.
socratic_hints: What is the angle $\theta$ between the dipole axis and the line joining the center to point $P$?
Does point $P$ lie along the axial line or at an arbitrary angle $\theta$?
Recall how the electric field components $E_r$ and $E_\theta$ depend on $\cos\theta$ and $\sin\theta$.

similar_pyqs.question_latex: An electric dipole of moment $\vec{p}$ is placed at origin. Find potential at $(r, \theta = 60^\circ)$.
